themes_detail.label: Standing water crisis
themes_detail.summary: Standing water complaints spiked to 4 reports THIS WEEK versus a baseline of 0.1 per week over the prior 8 weeks—a 3,100% increase (z-score: 11.72)—suggesting either a major drainage failure, flooding event, or sewage backup affecting multiple Lower Manhattan blocks.
evidence: 4 standing water complaints THIS WEEK vs. 0.1 weekly average over prior 8 weeks (3,100% spike)
Z-score of 11.72 indicates statistical anomaly at highest tier
No prior pattern; suggests acute event rather than chronic issue
reporting_angles: Which specific streets or neighborhoods are affected; is there a common cause (main break, storm drain failure, construction)?
Has DEP or DSNY confirmed root cause; what is the timeline for remediation?

themes_detail.label: Boiler failures surge
themes_detail.summary: Boiler complaints jumped to 3 reports last week versus a baseline of 0.2 per week—a 1,100% increase (z-score: 4.16)—raising concerns about widespread heating system failures in residential or commercial buildings during a critical season.
evidence: 3 boiler complaints last week vs. 0.2 weekly average over prior 8 weeks (1,100% spike)
Z-score of 4.16 indicates high statistical significance
Timing suggests potential seasonal neglect or aging infrastructure failures
reporting_angles: How many residential buildings are currently without heat; are any violations filed with HPD?
Are landlords using the spike to avoid repairs, or is there a systemic equipment failure pattern?

themes_detail.label: Dead animal accumulation
themes_detail.summary: Dead animal complaints hit 4 reports last week compared to a baseline of 0.5 per week—a 700% surge (z-score: 4.04)—indicating possible public health or sanitation failures affecting street cleanliness and pest control.
evidence: 4 dead animal complaints last week vs. 0.5 weekly average over prior 8 weeks (700% spike)
Converges with street cleanliness concerns implicit in chronic vendor enforcement and street condition complaints
reporting_angles: Which districts or streets are seeing the most reports; is DSNY pickup delayed?
Is there an underlying rodent or pest outbreak driving the increase?

themes_detail.label: Construction and plumbing surge
themes_detail.summary: General construction and plumbing complaints rose to 28 reports last week versus a baseline of 7.4 per week—a 280% increase (z-score: 8.61)—correlating with the 1,220 active DOB permits filed and suggesting widespread building work disruption or code violations.
evidence: 28 construction/plumbing complaints last week vs. 7.4 weekly average over prior 8 weeks (280% spike)
Z-score of 8.61 indicates high statistical significance
1,220 active DOB permits filed in last 90 days (1,047 alterations) suggest heavy concurrent construction activity
reporting_angles: Are contractors operating without proper permits or violating noise/hours restrictions?
Is the surge tied to specific large projects (Franklin Street, 65 Franklin, or 101 Franklin developments)?

themes_detail.label: Outdoor dining chaos
themes_detail.summary: Outdoor dining complaints spiked to 5 reports last week versus a baseline of 1.0 per week—a 400% increase (z-score: 4.0)—suggesting overcrowding, safety, or sanitation issues with sidewalk seating as the district rebounds post-pandemic.
evidence: 5 outdoor dining complaints last week vs. 1.0 weekly average over prior 8 weeks (400% spike)
Consistent with long-running concern about street quality (637 complaints over 90 days) and illegal parking (1,326 complaints)
reporting_angles: Which restaurants or blocks are generating complaints; are permits being enforced?
Are outdoor shed structures blocking pedestrian access or creating accessibility violations?
